Customer Verification: Integration Guide

blocks.raw: This guide walks through the full integration step by step, with example code for each stage. All code examples reference KYC (Know Your Customer) scenarios, but the same pattern applies to KYB (Know Your Business) applications.
blocks.text: This guide walks through the full integration step by step, with example code for each stage. All code examples reference KYC (Know Your Customer) scenarios, but the same pattern applies to KYB (Know Your Business) applications.
Step 1: Create an Application

blocks.raw: Before the SDK can be invoked, create an application instance for each customer via the Create Application API. Store the returned `id` against your customer record - it is used in all subsequent API calls and webhooks.
blocks.text: Before the SDK can be invoked, create an application instance for each customer via the Create Application API. Store the returned id against your customer record - it is used in all subsequent API calls and webhooks.

blocks.raw: > **Note:** Create a separate application for each business a customer wishes to onboard, even if ownership is identical across businesses.
blocks.text: Note: Create a separate application for each business a customer wishes to onboard, even if ownership is identical across businesses.
Response (201 Created)

blocks.raw: ## Step 2: Submit KYC/KYB Data via API (Optional)
blocks.text: Step 2: Submit KYC/KYB Data via API (Optional)

blocks.raw: Skip this step if you are using the SDK-only route. Jump straight to [Step 5](https://modulr.readme.io/docs/customer?isFramePreview=true#step-5-create-a-short-lived-token).
blocks.text: Skip this step if you are using the SDK-only route. Jump straight to Step 5.

blocks.raw: If you hold verified customer data already and want to reduce friction in the onboarding journey, you can pre-populate compliance data via the API before invoking the SDK.
blocks.text: If you hold verified customer data already and want to reduce friction in the onboarding journey, you can pre-populate compliance data via the API before invoking the SDK.
Create a Compliance Associate

blocks.raw: Submit identity data for each individual (the primary customer or associated individuals for a business application).
blocks.text: Submit identity data for each individual (the primary customer or associated individuals for a business application).
Response (201 Created)

blocks.raw: **Associate types:** Use `INDIVIDUAL` for KYC. For business applications, available types include `DIRECTOR`, `PARTNER`, `BENE_OWNER`, and `SOLETRADER`.
blocks.text: Associate types: Use INDIVIDUAL for KYC. For business applications, available types include DIRECTOR, PARTNER, BENE_OWNER, and SOLETRADER.
Submit KYB/KYC Data

blocks.raw: Provide expected activity details for the customer's Modulr account.
blocks.text: Provide expected activity details for the customer's Modulr account.
Response: 204 No Content
Submit Associate Personal Info

blocks.raw: Provide nationality data for the associate.
blocks.text: Provide nationality data for the associate.
Response: 204 No Content
Submit Associate Tax Residencies
Response: 204 No Content
Step 3: Handle APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE Webhooks

blocks.raw: Once the customer starts entering data, Modulr sends `APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE` webhook events to your registered endpoint. You must process these throughout the entire application lifecycle.
blocks.text: Once the customer starts entering data, Modulr sends APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE webhook events to your registered endpoint. You must process these throughout the entire application lifecycle.

blocks.raw: See the full webhook reference: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://modulr.readme.io/docs/webhook-application-status-change">Webhook - Application Status Change</Anchor>
blocks.text: See the full webhook reference: Webhook - Application Status Change

blocks.raw: Your webhook handler must be **idempotent** - the same event may be delivered more than once. Respond with `HTTP 200` to acknowledge receipt. Modulr will retry on failure.
blocks.text: Your webhook handler must be idempotent - the same event may be delivered more than once. Respond with HTTP 200 to acknowledge receipt. Modulr will retry on failure.

blocks.raw: ## Step 4 (optional): [Upload ID verification docs / biometric selfie image](https://modulr.readme.io/reference/uploaddocument)
blocks.text: Step 4 (optional): Upload ID verification docs / biometric selfie image

blocks.raw: We would generally always recommend that any documents that are used as part of the KYB/C application are being uploaded via our Customer Verification SDK (steps 6-9) to maximise the best chance of an automated approval, however, if you are already capturing these documents through your own providers for other purposes, you have the optional route of providing these documents/selfie captured images via API.
blocks.text: We would generally always recommend that any documents that are used as part of the KYB/C application are being uploaded via our Customer Verification SDK (steps 6-9) to maximise the best chance of an automated approval, however, if you are already capturing these documents through your own providers for other purposes, you have the optional route of providing these documents/selfie captured images via API.
Response (201 Created)
Step 5: Initiate Application Verification

blocks.raw: If you submitted data via the API in Step 2, call the verify endpoint to trigger Modulr's CDD orchestration. If you used the SDK-only route, the SDK makes this call automatically.
blocks.text: If you submitted data via the API in Step 2, call the verify endpoint to trigger Modulr's CDD orchestration. If you used the SDK-only route, the SDK makes this call automatically.
No request body required.
Response: 200 OK

blocks.raw: After this call, monitor `APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE` webhooks. The application will transition to one of:
blocks.text: After this call, monitor APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE webhooks. The application will transition to one of:

blocks.raw:
* `APPROVED` - all KYB/KYC checks passed
* `PENDING_STEP_UP` - further information required from the customer
* `MANUAL_REVIEW` - application queued for human review
blocks.text: APPROVED - all KYB/KYC checks passedPENDING_STEP_UP - further information required from the customerMANUAL_REVIEW - application queued for human review
Step 6: Create a Short-lived Token

blocks.raw: Before initialising the SDK, request a short-lived token and HMAC from the Modulr keys endpoint.
blocks.text: Before initialising the SDK, request a short-lived token and HMAC from the Modulr keys endpoint.

blocks.raw: > **Important:** This call must be made server-side. Never expose the token or HMAC in client-side code or logs.
blocks.text: Important: This call must be made server-side. Never expose the token or HMAC in client-side code or logs.
Response (201 Created)

blocks.raw: The token has a short TTL. Request a fresh token immediately before each SDK initialisation.
blocks.text: The token has a short TTL. Request a fresh token immediately before each SDK initialisation.

blocks.raw: ## Step 7: Initialise the Customer Verification SDK
blocks.text: Step 7: Initialise the Customer Verification SDK

blocks.raw: Use the token, HMAC, and application ID from the previous steps to initialise the SDK.
blocks.text: Use the token, HMAC, and application ID from the previous steps to initialise the SDK.
Custom Styling (Optional)

blocks.raw: The SDK supports visual customisation to match your product's design system. All styling properties are optional - omit the block entirely to use Modulr defaults.
blocks.text: The SDK supports visual customisation to match your product's design system. All styling properties are optional - omit the block entirely to use Modulr defaults.
Only call open() (Step 7) after onInit fires successfully.

blocks.raw: ## Step 8: Open the Customer Verification SDK
blocks.text: Step 8: Open the Customer Verification SDK

blocks.raw: Call `open()` once the SDK has initialised. The SDK can be displayed as a modal (default) or embedded inline in a container element.
blocks.text: Call open() once the SDK has initialised. The SDK can be displayed as a modal (default) or embedded inline in a container element.
Modal mode (default)
Inline / embedded mode

blocks.raw: `containerId` must reference a visible DOM element. Use `onClose` to clean up your UI when the customer exits the SDK.
blocks.text: containerId must reference a visible DOM element. Use onClose to clean up your UI when the customer exits the SDK.
Step 9: Close the SDK

blocks.raw: The SDK can be closed programmatically at any time.
blocks.text: The SDK can be closed programmatically at any time.

blocks.raw: The `onClose` callback registered in `open()` fires whether the SDK is closed by the user or programmatically.
blocks.text: The onClose callback registered in open() fires whether the SDK is closed by the user or programmatically.
Step 10: Handle PENDING_STEP_UP

blocks.raw: If further information is required after initial submission, Modulr sends an `APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE` webhook with status `PENDING_STEP_UP`.
blocks.text: If further information is required after initial submission, Modulr sends an APPLICATION_STATUS_CHANGE webhook with status PENDING_STEP_UP.
When you receive this:

blocks.raw:
1. Notify your customer that further information is required.
2. Re-invoke the SDK (repeat <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://modulr.readme.io/docs/customer?isFramePreview=true#step-5-create-a-short-lived-token">Steps 6-9</Anchor>) using the same `applicationId`. A fresh short-lived token is required for each invocation.
3. The SDK will automatically surface the step-up form for the outstanding requirements.
blocks.text: Notify your customer that further information is required.Re-invoke the SDK (repeat Steps 6-9) using the same applicationId. A fresh short-lived token is required for each invocation.The SDK will automatically surface the step-up form for the outstanding requirements.

blocks.raw: This applies both after automated CDD checks and after a manual review decision - meaning these notifications could come back within a few seconds for automated step-ups, or hours/days after the initial submission depending on the complexity of the manual review.
blocks.text: This applies both after automated CDD checks and after a manual review decision - meaning these notifications could come back within a few seconds for automated step-ups, or hours/days after the initial submission depending on the complexity of the manual review.
Step 11: Receive CUSTOMER_CREATED

blocks.raw: Once the application reaches `APPROVED` status, Modulr sends a `CUSTOMER_CREATED` webhook containing the new `customerId`.
blocks.text: Once the application reaches APPROVED status, Modulr sends a CUSTOMER_CREATED webhook containing the new customerId.

blocks.raw: Store the `customerId` against your customer record. Use it in subsequent <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://modulr.readme.io/reference/createaccount">Account Creation API</Anchor> calls.
blocks.text: Store the customerId against your customer record. Use it in subsequent Account Creation API calls.

blocks.raw: See the full webhook reference: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://modulr.readme.io/docs/webhook-customer-created">Webhook - Customer Created</Anchor>
blocks.text: See the full webhook reference: Webhook - Customer Created
Step 12: Monitor CUSTOMER_STATUS_CHANGE

blocks.raw: Once a customer is live on Modulr, monitor the `CUSTOMER_STATUS_CHANGE` webhook to track ongoing lifecycle events, including `BLOCKED` status which prevents payment processing.
blocks.text: Once a customer is live on Modulr, monitor the CUSTOMER_STATUS_CHANGE webhook to track ongoing lifecycle events, including BLOCKED status which prevents payment processing.

blocks.raw: See the full webhook reference: <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://modulr.readme.io/docs/customer-status">Webhook - Customer Status Change</Anchor>
blocks.text: See the full webhook reference: Webhook - Customer Status Change
